sections.heading: Preamble
sections.summary: The Preamble establishes the authority of the people of Rwanda and their commitment to unity, democracy, and respect for human rights.

sections.heading: Sovereignty
sections.summary: Rwanda is a sovereign democratic republic where all power belongs to the people, exercised through elections or referendums.

sections.heading: Territory
sections.summary: Rwanda's territory includes its land from 1962, internal waters, airspace, and subsoil, with maritime boundaries defined by international law.

sections.heading: National Language and Other Official Languages
sections.summary: Kinyarwanda is the national language. Kinyarwanda, English, and French are official languages. Swahili may be used in specific legal circumstances.

sections.heading: National Symbols
sections.summary: Rwanda's national symbols are the flag, anthem, coat of arms, and seal, defined by law. Desecration is punishable.

sections.heading: Capital City
sections.summary: Kigali is the capital city of Rwanda.

sections.heading: Separation of Powers
sections.summary: Rwanda's government has three separate but complementary branches: Executive, Legislature, and Judiciary, each with defined responsibilities.

sections.heading: Supremacy of the Constitution
sections.summary: The Constitution is the supreme law. All laws and government actions must comply with it. Anything inconsistent with the Constitution is invalid.

sections.heading: Direct Application of the Constitution
sections.summary: The Constitution applies directly to everyone in Rwanda, including all government institutions and individuals.

sections.heading: Hierarchy of Legal Norms
sections.summary: The Constitution is the highest law, followed by organic laws, ordinary laws, and various orders. Higher-level laws override lower-level ones in conflicts.

documents.rightsNotes: Law No. 055/2024 of 20/06/2024, Article 282 (published and effective 31/07/2024) explicitly excludes official legislative, administrative and judicial texts and official translations from copyright protection. The Constitution of the Republic of Rwanda is an official legislative text published in the Official Gazette. The Rwanda Law Reform Commission maintains the Laws of Rwanda collection (updated daily) which includes the Constitution under laws in force. Both RLRC and Parliament host identical trilingual copies (Kinyarwanda, English, French). This statutory exclusion has been reviewed and confirmed to cover CARTA's intended uses: full-text web/mobile display, indexing for search, AI retrieval and embeddings for legal research, and offline device caching. Legal opinion on file confirms applicability to the exact constitutional text and all CARTA use cases.
